trace.notes: Normalized ARGUMENTS as one zbMATH resolver URL with identifier 7495237.

Direct shell access to the zbMATH page encountered Cloudflare challenge/DNS failures. The zbMATH REST API record for 7495237 identified the exact title, author Michel Boyom, pages 380-388, and DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-80209-7_42.

The DOI resolved to a Springer landing page with only abstract, references, and purchase/subscription options visible. OpenAlex reported the DOI as closed access with no best OA location and no repository full text. Exact-work search recovered a full HTML transcription of the same GSI 2021 proceedings volume on DOKUMEN; the chapter title, author, pages, and DOI matched the zbMATH/Crossref record, so that HTML artifact was used as the readable primary source.

Mapped the HTML chapter: title and abstract; Section 1 Notation and Basic Notions, including 1.1 Differential Structure Versus Parameterization, 1.2 C-infinity Relation, 1.3 Geometric Structure Versus Topology of Fibrations, 1.4 Equations of (X,P(X)), 1.5 Structured Foliations, and 1.6 Open Problems; Section 2 Relevant Geometric Structures Which Impact the Information Geometry; Section 3 The Aim of the Talk; Section 3.1 Long-Awaited Characteristic Obstructions; references.

Sections 1.1 through 1.4 define parameterizations, C-infinity relations, geometric structures, jets, and equations of G-structures; no standalone open question block was accepted from these definitional subsections.
Extracted the structured-foliation existence schema from the definition of structured foliation and the EXF(S > M) existence statement.

Extracted the broad geometric-structure existence question, the structured S-foliation question, the applied information-geometry structure question, and the machine-learning poll-sample discretization candidate.
Extracted the explicit list of still-open existence problems for locally flat, symplectic, almost complex, Hessian, left-invariant, two-sided invariant, and structured foliation settings.
Extracted the Riemannian-foliation construction question and marked it solved because the source explicitly says the new numerical invariants yield complete solutions of that question.
Rewrote the locally flat entry as a standalone existence question for a differentiable manifold M.
Rewrote the symplectic entry as a standalone existence question for a differentiable manifold M.
Rewrote the almost complex entry as a standalone existence question for a differentiable manifold M.
Rewrote the Hessian-in-Riemannian-manifold entry as a standalone question for a Riemannian manifold (M,g).
Rewrote the Hessian-in-locally-flat-manifold entry as a standalone question for a locally flat manifold (M,nabla).
Rewrote the left-invariant locally flat entry as a standalone existence question for a finite-dimensional Lie group G.
Rewrote the left-invariant symplectic entry as a standalone existence question for a finite-dimensional Lie group G.
Rewrote the left-invariant Hessian entry as a standalone existence question for a finite-dimensional Lie group G.
Rewrote the two-sided invariant Riemannian entry as a standalone existence question for a finite-dimensional Lie group G.
Expanded structured S-foliation using the source definition that its leaves uniformly carry the prescribed structure S.
Rewrote the applied information-geometry version as an existence question for prescribed geometric or topological structures on a complex system or Big Data object.
Rewrote the Riemannian-foliation construction prompt as a standalone question and carried forward the source's explicit complete-solution claim into solved-status metadata.

Did not accept the poll-sample discretization candidate because the source does not define poll samples, coarse foliations, or discretization of a prescribed structured foliation sufficiently for a self-contained rewrite.

Merged the broad EX(S > M) geometric-structure existence schema into the more specific accepted existence questions q_001 through q_009. Merged the repeated structured-foliation mentions into q_010. Kept q_011 because it is the applied information-geometry version, and kept q_012 because the source separately states the Riemannian-foliation construction question and a solution claim.

Accepted q_001 through q_012 passed schema, evidence locator, no-new-facts, and source-adequacy checks. The terse source list does not define every standard geometric structure, so the rewrites preserve the source terminology without adding unsupported formal definitions. q_013 was moved to needs_review for undefined terminology.
